text: To-day: Helen is back at Stoke Moran, waiting eagerly for Holmes and Watson
why: Helen said she would return by the twelve o'clock train; she is at Stoke Moran and says she has been waiting eagerly.

text: That afternoon: Holmes and Watson come to Stoke Moran as promised, and Miss Stoner hurries to meet them
why: Holmes greets her with 'Good-afternoon' and says they have kept their word; she hurries forward to meet them.

text: This evening at the earliest: Dr. Roylott is expected back
why: Paraphrases Helen's statement that it is unlikely he will be back before evening.

text: When will Dr. Roylott come back to Stoke Moran?
why: A plain question raised by Helen's remark about his absence and the need to inspect the rooms without his knowledge.

text: When will Dr. Roylott come back to Stoke Moran? — not before evening
why: This is what Helen says is likely.

text: When will Dr. Roylott come back to Stoke Moran? — sooner than she expects, while the rooms are being examined
id: q.roylott_back=sooner than she expects, while the rooms are being examined
why: A reasonable possibility: Helen's estimate is only a probability, the visit must be kept from him, and he has already shown he is tracking her movements. It reveals nothing later.
